text:
Tess G: hi all, day 1 here. i followed the onboarding and merged kubeconfigs. i can see contexts but when i `kubectl create ns dev-tess` i get a quota error: 
```\nError from server (Forbidden): namespaces \"dev-tess\" is forbidden: exceeded quota: namespace-count, requested: namespaces=1, used: namespaces=20, limited: namespaces=20\n```
Tess G: also when i `kubectl auth can-i create pods -n rl-ml` it returns `no` and the error mentions `system:serviceaccount:default:tess-sa` which surprised me.
Ben (DevEx): welcome! two separate things: quota is an infra policy, and the SA mention usually comes from a merged kubeconfig referencing a serviceaccount. run `kubectl config get-contexts` and `kubectl config view users -o jsonpath='{.users[*].name}'` to check which user is attached to your context.
Tess G: `kubectl config get-contexts` shows my context `redwood-dev` with USER `tess@example.com` but users list includes `system:serviceaccount:default:tess-sa` too. i probably merged a CI kubeconfig.
Ben (DevEx): yup. quick fix: set the context user back to your email: `kubectl config set-context redwood-dev --user=tess@example.com`. For quota, infra tracks personal namespace count. Sam, can infra either bump the quota or provision a namespace for Tess?
Sam K: infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7340 to provision `dev-tess` and to review namespace quotas (priority: normal). i can also provision a scoped sandbox if the quota is tight.
identity-bot: Identity sync for tess@example.com: completed, groups: [team-ml].
Tess G: interesting that identity sync completed but `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n rl-ml` still returns `no`.
Ben (DevEx): sometimes the RBAC RoleBindings reference group emails differently. run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n rl-ml --as=tess@example.com` and also check with `--as=system:serviceaccount:default:tess-sa` to confirm which account is blocked.
Tess G: `--as=tess@example.com` -> no, `--as=system:serviceaccount:default:tess-sa` -> no as well. what should i do next?
Ben (DevEx): ok. two debugging steps: (1) ask infra to provision a personal namespace so you can progress while we sort team RBAC; (2) Sam can check the NamespaceRoleBinding in rl-ml to ensure `team-ml` maps to the same group name that identity-sync emits. Sam, can you inspect the RoleBindings?
Sam K: checking... rl-ml has RoleBinding `team-ml-edit` that binds Group `ml-team` (note: underscore mismatch). that explains it  identity sync emits `team-ml` with a dash. i'll open a ticket to fix the binding mapping. infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-7341 to update RoleBinding in rl-ml to include group `team-ml`.
Sam K: meanwhile INFRA-7340 created dev-tess namespace and bound `edit` to tess-sa. try `kubectl auth can-i create deployments -n dev-tess`.
Tess G: that returns `yes` and i can deploy the sample. thanks!
Ben (DevEx): follow-up doc: we added a small section to onboarding about checking RoleBinding group names vs identity sync group naming. check https://redwood.dev/onboarding/k8s-access (kubeconfig merge and identity mapping). short checklist for new hires: (1) verify `kubectl config get-contexts` and USER column, (2) if you see unexpected SAs, switch the context user back to your email, (3) run `kubectl auth can-i` before opening an INFRA ticket, (4) request a personal namespace if quota or RBAC blocks you.
Tess G: great, deploying now. appreciate the quick responses! :smile:
